correctness.rationale: The quandle product becomes F star G=sigma_{-1}(F)sigma_2(G) in the ordinary truncated group algebra. Augmentation-zero solutions vanish by doubling the y-adic filtration, valid over any field. Augmentation-one solutions are linearized by the ordinary truncated log/exp group isomorphism on 1+(y), since the ideal has nilpotency p and denominators below p are units. The logarithmic generator t=log X diagonalizes sigma_{-1} and sigma_2 with eigenvalues (-1)^j and 2^j; hence exactly the odd j with ord_p(2) dividing j-1 survive. Independent basis-multiplication exhaustive tests for p=3 and 5 and seeded constructed tests for p=7,11,17,31 returned VERIFY_OK. Finite tests do not replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: The exact characteristic-matched modular description for every odd prime p, including the logarithmic coordinate law and prime-dependent higher-dimensional jumps, is not implication-covered by inspected prior work. The 2022 full text treats specific small quandle rings; Churchill et al. (arXiv:2608.09149v1) treat Core(D_3) and integral examples, not modular Core(C_p) for all p. The August/September 2026 integral-quandle conclusions use integral coefficient rings; they do not imply this positive-characteristic classification. The published characteristic-three R_3 result is an explicitly acknowledged special case, not a new result. Residual risk includes incompletely accessed September full texts and unindexed historical equivalents.
residual_risks: The full texts and appendices of arXiv:2609.03799v1 and arXiv:2609.09183v1 were unavailable. Their abstracts target the integral coefficient setting, but cannot conclusively exclude an unadvertised modular corollary.
Older unindexed results may use the group-ring cocycle equation F=F(X^{-1})F(X^2) or a different parameterization without quandle terminology.
The characteristic-three R_3 case was already established; the claimed novel contribution starts with the all-prime order-of-two stratification.

value.rationale: The characteristic-matched modular dihedral quandle algebras are a natural infinite family in a recent active classification problem. The theorem describes their entire idempotent loci, not just selected solutions, using a structural logarithmic eigenspace model. The order of 2 modulo p governs a nontrivial jump to two parameters at p=17 and three at p=31, yielding exact finite-field counts and higher-dimensional affine families that cannot be inferred from the earlier p=3 case. Such explicit modular idempotents provide a natural input for quandle-algebra idempotent questions and constructions, without claiming new knot invariants or a paper-sized general downstream theorem.
